title: Finding support after baby loss | NHS inform
text:
Finding support after baby loss
If you’re struggling to cope after your loss, you should first speak to your GP. They want to hear from you, and will help you get the support you need.
Speak to your GP practice if:
You or someone else has symptoms of depression like:
continuous low mood or sadness
lack of motivation
feeling hopeless and helpless
feeling anxious or worried
disturbed sleep
avoiding contact with family and friends
feeling overwhelmed by daily life and the needs of your home, work or family life
There are organisations across Scotland that provide support after pregnancy loss. They can help with various things, including giving you someone to talk to or providing information about what happens next.
You can also look at their online resources. Some of the organisations provide helplines, online forums and support groups.
Where to find support
Held In Our Hearts
provides pregnancy loss counselling and support for families. Counselling is free and open ended.
Miscarriage Association
offers support to those affected by miscarriage, ectopic pregnancy or molar pregnancy. Their services include a helpline, live chat, support groups and leaflets.
Sands
is an organisation for anyone who has been affected by the loss of a baby. It runs a helpline and an email help service, as well as providing information about baby loss.
SiMBA
provides memory boxes, family rooms in hospitals and remembrance events.
Tommy’s
provides information and support for everyone affected by pregnancy loss.
Twins Trust
offers support for families who have lost one or more children from a multiple birth.
ARC
offers bereavement support and information for parents who choose to end a pregnancy after a medical diagnosis.
Baby Loss Retreat
offers aftercare support to families who have suffered the loss of a baby. It hosts free retreats throughout Scotland. These provide a quiet environment where parents can reflect on their loss.
Child Bereavement UK
supports families when a baby or child of any age dies or is dying. They can also help when a child is facing bereavement.
Cruse Scotland Bereavement Support
provides professional support for bereaved people across Scotland.
Ectopic Pregnancy Trust
provides support for people affected by ectopic pregnancy. This includes information resources, a helpline and a forum.
Relationships Scotland
offers counselling services for every type of relationship. You can have face-to-face, telephone and online counselling, either alone or as a couple.
MISS
provides support for parents in Scotland after miscarriage. They’re based in Aberdeenshire, but their online services are available across Scotland.
